V22 · Convective downdraft wind-potential experiment

Compares actual HRRR 15-minute gusts with the idealized parcel energy speed calculated from existing HRRR/GFS DCAPE soundings. This is a conditional physics sensitivity, not a validated surface-gust forecast.

0–30% is a user-controlled sensitivity range, NOT an empirically calibrated downdraft efficiency. No automatic change to operational outage curves.
Load 15-minute HRRR data and the atmospheric sounding profiles to compare coincident data.
Illustration: potential = √(GUST² + η × 2 × DCAPE × 2.23694²), with gust in mph and DCAPE in J/kg. This energy-combination assumption has not been validated against CU storm gust observations; it is not a deterministic thunderstorm gust prediction. CAPE, precipitation and shear are environmental context, not proof of a downdraft. No extra outage total is added.
Convective-wind qualification · bounded integration

Uses the same sounding state as the DCAPE experiment and evaluates every 15-minute interval before allowing the experimental DCAPE wind-potential line. A qualified interval requires either a native HRRR thunderstorm weather code, or the simultaneous overlap of modeled precipitation + CAPE ≥500 J/kg + time-matched DCAPE. This is a research gate, not a validated severe-wind algorithm. V28 waits for a READY sounding/DCAPE state, then sends only qualified potential into the main outage chart; the integration is max(native HRRR wind-only impact, historical convective analogue), never an additive total.

Load HRRR wind/CAPE and sounding data to evaluate the gate.
Gate labels: STORM CODE = native HRRR weather code 95–99. PRECIP+CAPE+DCAPE = precipitation at ≥1 of 12 sites, maximum sampled CAPE ≥500 J/kg, and a time-matched DCAPE sounding. FAIL labels identify the missing ingredient. Gold wind potential is drawn only for qualified intervals. On the main outage chart, qualified convective curves rise vertically from zero at the first qualified interval and return vertically to zero at the last qualified interval; no zero-level line is drawn outside the qualified window. Operational outage curves remain unchanged.

V12 · verified gust-product definitions and NOAA field inventory
Open-Meteo GFS/NAM/HRRR wind_gusts_10m: preceding-hour maximum gust (the existing input). NOAA HRRR GUST: modeled gust at forecast hour. NOAA HRRR WIND at 10 m with 1–2 hour max: maximum wind speed over that hour, not a gust. NOAA MAXUW/MAXVW are components of hourly maximum wind and must not be interpreted as gusts.
No new numerical wind field is integrated in V12. The outage equations remain unchanged. A positive inventory check proves the field is listed, not that its GRIB2 values were retrieved, decoded, or suitable for replacing gusts.

Data connection notes (expand)

The four status checks attempt to read NOAA public GRIB2 inventory files (including NOAA open-data cloud mirrors where available) (.idx) from the most recent scheduled cycles. NOAA may restrict cross-origin browser requests; if blocked, the indicator remains red instead of falsely reporting a healthy data feed. Browser security may prevent direct access. No software installation is required to view or test this dashboard; actual GRIB2 decoding and automatic chart updates are not implemented.

Next expected run is calculated from NOAA's published model initialization cadence, not guaranteed file-publication time. Next available data remains pending until NOAA actually publishes the run and it is successfully checked. HRRR normally updates hourly; GFS, NAM and NAM Nest initialize at 00, 06, 12 and 18 UTC. Processing and publication lag varies.

V29 · Historical storm calibration & live-risk cross-check

Current NWS Springfield outlook (Oct 13, 2026): Showers and thunderstorms tonight through Thursday night; isolated severe storms may produce 60 mph gusts. This official hazard scenario is not the HRRR point gust or a calibrated CU outage forecast. Read latest NWS hazardous weather outlook ↗. NWS discussion ↗

Calibration requires observed gusts from past events paired with model gust and DCAPE at the same location/time. CU outage counts can be included for independent impact validation. No historical values are prefilled or fabricated. Results remain research-only; V28 operational equations are unchanged.

No historical events evaluated. Two or more independent events are needed for even a preliminary comparison; 10–20+ recommended for fitting.

Method: fits η in observed_gust² ≈ model_gust² + η × 2 × DCAPE × 2.23694², constrained 0–0.30; compares 0%, 10%, fitted η with MAE, plus leave-one-out MAE where ≥3 events. This is an empirical sensitivity check, not a validated downdraft physics law. It does not use outage counts to fit gusts; no extrapolated confidence intervals. CSV stays in this browser's local storage when supported.
